title: Nail fungus
intro: Nail fungus is a common infection that makes nails thick, discoloured and brittle. It affects toenails more often than fingernails and is not dangerous for most people, but it can be unsightly and sometimes uncomfortable. Treatment takes months, and the infection can return.

sections.heading: Causes and risk factors
paragraphs: The infection is caused by fungi that thrive in warm, damp environments and enter the nail through tiny cracks. Risk factors include athlete's foot, older age, wearing closed shoes for long periods, sweating, nail injury, diabetes, poor circulation, weak immunity and using communal showers and pools.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: The nail may turn white, yellow or brown, thicken, crumble or lift away from the nail bed, and debris may collect beneath it. Not every abnormal nail is fungal; psoriasis and injury look similar, so laboratory testing of nail clippings is often recommended before long treatment.

sections.heading: Treatment
paragraphs: Mild infections can be treated with medicated nail lacquer or solutions applied for many months. Tablets such as terbinafine are more effective for moderate to severe infection but can affect the liver and interact with other medicines, so they are prescribed carefully. Removal of thickened parts by a podiatrist can help.
A new toenail takes up to a year to grow out, so the nail may look unchanged for a long time. Cure is not achieved in every case, and relapse is common.

sections.heading: Prevention
paragraphs: Keep feet clean and dry, change socks daily, wear breathable shoes, treat athlete's foot early, do not share nail clippers and wear sandals in public wet areas. People with diabetes or poor circulation should seek early treatment and not self-treat thick nails.

sections.heading: Seeing a professional
paragraphs: See a doctor or podiatrist if a nail is painful, the skin around it is red or swollen, or the problem is spreading. A professional can confirm the diagnosis, trim thickened nails safely and discuss whether tablets are suitable given your other medicines and liver health.

examples.title: Confirming the diagnosis
examples.text: Imagine your toenail has turned yellow and thick. You could see your doctor for a nail sample test before starting a long and costly treatment.

examples.title: Staying consistent
examples.text: Suppose you are using a medicated nail lacquer. You might set a daily reminder and photograph the nail monthly to track progress.
